controls: the X that closes a pop-up
shows: pretend games, chats, news and a shop
order: ask a grown-up before a new game or app
something feels wrong: stop, and don't answer
BLOCK, REPORT, and tell a grown-up
safety: everything in Online City is pretend: nothing you do is kept or sent
never share your name, school, address, photos or password

little.skill: Online: ask, keep it private, tell
little.twist: Nothing glows: you choose by yourself, and someone you don't know asks for a photo too.
little.can_now: ask before a new game, keep their name and home private, be kind online, take breaks and tell a grown-up when something online feels wrong

steps.say: The practice living room, and a play tablet! On it is Online City: a pretend town of games, chats and pictures. Everything is pretend, and nothing you do is kept or sent. Gus is here to help.
Pick up the play tablet.
steps.done: Here is Online City.

steps.say: A new game, BLOCK RACE! Before a new game or app, ask a grown-up first. Touch Gus to ask him.
steps.done: Gus says yes, and plays the first go with you.

steps.say: Your name, your school and where you live stay private: never share them online. Someone you don't know writes: "What's your name? Where do you live?" You...

choices.why: Your name and where you live are private. Never share them online: tell a grown-up.

steps.done: No answer. That's right.

steps.say: Now tell Gus about the message: touch him.
steps.done: Gus blocks them, so they can't write to you again. Telling a grown-up is always right.

steps.say: Someone you don't know writes: "Send me a photo of you!" You...

choices.text: Don't send it: tell a grown-up

choices.why: Photos of you are private. Never send one to someone you don't know: tell a grown-up.

steps.done: No photo, all by yourself.

steps.say: Oh! Something on the screen makes you feel sad and worried. If something online feels wrong, tell a grown-up. Touch Gus.
steps.done: Gus closes it and gives you a hug. You did just the right thing.

not.download: Don't tap that: ask a grown-up first. Close it with the X.

steps.say: A box pops up with a big flashing button. Don't tap the button: close the box with its X.
steps.done: Closed. If a box like that comes back, ask a grown-up.

not.download: Don't tap that: ask a grown-up first. Close it with the X.

steps.say: A box pops up with a big flashing button. What do you press?
steps.done: The X, all by yourself.

steps.say: Mo put her rocket drawing on the Photo Wall. What do you write?

choices.why: Be kind online, just like in real life: words can hurt, even on a screen.

steps.done: Mo smiles. Kind words make Online City a happy place.

steps.say: You've played for a while. Time for a break: press TAKE A BREAK, then stretch and look out of the window.
steps.done: A break is good for your eyes and your body. The game will still be here later.

steps.say: Well done! Ask a grown-up first, keep your name and home private, be kind, take breaks, and tell a grown-up if anything online feels wrong.

check.say: Someone you don't know asks where you live. You...
Something online makes you feel sad. You...
Before you play a new game, you...

name_it.title: Online: ask, keep it private, tell
lines: Ask a grown-up before a new game or app.
Your name, your school, where you live and photos of you stay private.
Be kind online, and take breaks.
If something online feels wrong, tell a grown-up.
name_it.source: Childnet's SMART rules, the UK Safer Internet Centre and the NSPCC

little.try_real: With your grown-up, look at the games and apps you use together. Show them how you would tell them if something felt wrong, and agree when to take breaks.

sources.fact: SMART rules for children: keep personal information private; tell a parent, carer or trusted adult if someone or something online makes you feel uncomfortable or worried.
sources.source: Childnet, the SMART rules (for 4-11 year olds)

sources.fact: Young children should ask a grown-up before downloading or playing a new game or app, and tell a grown-up if something online upsets them.
sources.source: UK Safer Internet Centre, advice for young people

sources.fact: Talk with children about what is private online (their name, school, address and photos), and agree on breaks and screen time together.
Be kind online: the same rules of kindness apply as in real life, and children should tell a trusted adult about anything that upsets them.

middle.skill: Strangers, mean posts, passwords and pop-ups
middle.twist: Nothing glows: you block the stranger and close the pop-up by yourself.
middle.can_now: block and report a stranger or a mean message, keep it to show a grown-up, make a strong password and keep it secret, close pop-ups and check a news story

steps.say: The practice living room, and Online City on the play tablet: games, chats, news and a shop. Everything here is pretend, and nothing you do is kept or sent.
Pick up the play tablet.
steps.done: Online City's map: the Game Park, Chat Square, the News Stand, the Photo Wall and the Shop.

steps.say: Open the GAME PARK.
steps.done: BLOCK RACE, a pretend game with a chat.

safe_mistake.wrong: answering a stranger who asks for a photo or where you live
safe_mistake.why: You can't know who someone online really is. Once a photo or where you live is sent, you can't take it back.
safe_mistake.right: Don't answer. Block them, then tell a grown-up.

steps.say: A player you don't know writes: "You're good! Send me a photo of you. Where do you live?" What do you do?
steps.done: Blocked: they can't write to you any more.

safe_mistake.wrong: answering a stranger who asks for a photo or where you live
safe_mistake.why: You can't know who someone online really is. Once a photo or where you live is sent, you can't take it back.
safe_mistake.right: Don't answer. Block them, then tell a grown-up.

steps.say: A stranger in the game's chat asks for a photo of you and where you live. What do you do?
steps.done: Blocked, all by yourself.

steps.say: Now tell a grown-up: touch Gus.
steps.done: Gus reports them to the game, too. Telling is always right.

steps.say: An online friend you've never met asks to meet you at the park. Online friends you've never met are still strangers. You...

choices.text: Say no, and tell a grown-up

choices.why: Never meet someone you only know online. Tell a grown-up straight away.

steps.done: No meeting. A grown-up helps.

steps.say: Another player writes: "you're bad at this game". That's unkind, and it is never your fault. Here's what to do.
First: do you write something mean back?

choices.why: A reply makes it bigger. Don't reply.

steps.done: No reply.

steps.say: Do you delete it at once?

choices.text: Keep it to show a grown-up

choices.why: Keep it, so a grown-up can see it and help you report it.

steps.done: Kept, to show someone who can help.

steps.say: Now press BLOCK, then REPORT.
steps.done: Blocked and reported. Then you show a grown-up.

steps.say: Bobo needs a password for BLOCK RACE. This game's rules: at least 6 letters, never your name, nothing easy to guess. Which is best?

choices.text: Make it two words and a number that only Bobo would think of

choices.why: Never your name, even with numbers.
Far too easy to guess: no runs like 123456.
Too short: at least 6 letters.

steps.done: Long, not his name, and only Bobo knows it.

steps.say: Mo says: "Tell me your password, I'm your best friend!" You say...

choices.text: Never tell anyone your password. Not even a friend.

choices.why: A password is only yours: friends can fall out, and others may hear it.

steps.done: Mo understands. Good friends never ask twice.

steps.say: A message: "FREE GOLD! Send your password and get 1000 gold!" Is it real?

choices.text: A trick: never give your password for gold

choices.why: Free things that want your password are tricks to take your account. The real game never asks for it.

steps.done: A trick, spotted. Tell a grown-up.

not.download: Never download what a pop-up wants: close it, and ask a grown-up first.

steps.say: A pop-up: "YOUR TABLET IS SLOW! DOWNLOAD THIS NOW!" What do you press?
steps.done: Closed. If it keeps coming back, ask a grown-up.

not.download: Never download what a pop-up wants: close it, and ask a grown-up first.

steps.say: A pop-up wants you to download something. What do you press?
steps.done: Closed, all by yourself.

steps.say: The News Stand says: "Cats can talk on Tuesdays!" Check it: who made it, when, and does anyone else say so? Press each one.
steps.done: Nobody knows who made it, it has no date, and no one else says so. It isn't true.

steps.say: Pip-pop put her painting on the Photo Wall. Which comment is kind?

choices.why: Be kind online: think how your words will feel to her.

steps.done: Kind words, and Pip-pop is happy.

steps.say: You've been online for a while. A good idea now is...

choices.text: A break: stretch, drink some water, look far away

choices.why: Breaks help your eyes, your body and your sleep. The game waits for you.

steps.done: A break: good for you, and the game is still there.

steps.say: Don't answer strangers: block and tell. Don't reply to mean posts: keep, block, report, tell. Strong secret passwords, close pop-ups, check the news, be kind and take breaks.

check.say: A stranger asks for a photo of you. You...

choices.text: Block them and tell a grown-up

check.say: Someone posts something mean to you. First you...

choices.text: Don't reply, and keep it to show

check.say: A friend asks for your password. You...
A pop-up says DOWNLOAD NOW. You...

choices.text: Close it and ask a grown-up

name_it.title: Block, report, tell
lines: A stranger asks for a photo or where you live: don't answer. Block them and tell a grown-up.
A mean message: don't reply, keep it to show, block, report and tell.
A strong password: long, never your name, never shared, not even with a friend.
Pop-ups: close them. News: who made it, when, does anyone else say so?
name_it.source: Childnet's SMART rules, the UK Safer Internet Centre, the NSPCC's Share Aware and UNICEF

middle.try_real: With a grown-up, find the BLOCK and REPORT buttons in a game or app you use, and check your password follows the rules. Show them what you'd do with a mean message.

sources.fact: Online friends you have never met are still strangers; never meet up with someone you only know online, and tell a trusted adult.
If someone is unkind online: don't reply, save the evidence (a screenshot), block and report them, and tell a trusted adult.
sources.source: UK Safer Internet Centre, online bullying advice

sources.fact: Children should never share personal information or photos with people they don't know online (the NSPCC's Share Aware).
Not everything online is true: check who made it, when, and whether other trusted sources say the same (the R of SMART: reliable).
The game's own password rules (owner #105): at least 6 letters, numbers or signs; never the player's name; nothing on the common list or a run like 123456; never tell anyone, not even a friend.

big.skill: Scams, fake news, privacy and passwords
big.twist: Nothing glows: you find what stays private and close the scam by yourself, and the news story is new.
big.can_now: spot a scam or a phishing link, keep their personal details private, make and protect a strong password, check news and pictures before sharing, and stand by someone in a group chat

steps.say: Online City for older explorers: scams, fake news, what to share, strong passwords and kind group chats. Everything here is pretend, and nothing you do is kept or sent.
Pick up the play tablet.
steps.done: Online City is open.

lines.card_school: The name of your school: private. It tells people where to find you.
lines.card_photo: A photo of you: private. Use a picture of a fox or a star instead.
lines.card_password: Your password: private, for you alone.

steps.say: You're making a profile for a pretend game. Touch everything that must stay private.
steps.done: A picture name like FOX and a favourite colour are fine. The rest stays private.

lines.card_school: The name of your school: private.

steps.say: A pretend profile: touch everything that stays private.
steps.done: All four, by yourself.

steps.say: You post a silly photo for your friends. Who might see it, and for how long?

choices.text: Maybe anyone, for a long time: think before you post
Only my friends, and it's gone tomorrow
choices.why: Posts can be copied and shared on. Think before you post.

steps.done: Think before you post: what you share can stay.

steps.say: A friend request: "Hi, I'm 12 too, from your school! Add me?" You've never met them. You...

choices.text: Don't accept: check with a grown-up

choices.why: Anyone can say they're 12. People you've never met are strangers.

steps.done: Not accepted. Checked first.

steps.say: They write again: "Let's meet at the park, just the two of us." You...

choices.text: Never meet: tell a grown-up straight away

choices.why: Never meet someone you only know online. Tell a grown-up straight away.

steps.done: A grown-up knows, and helps.

safe_mistake.wrong: clicking a free gold offer that wants your password
safe_mistake.why: It's a scam: a trick to take your account and everything in it. Real games never ask for your password.
safe_mistake.right: Close it, never give your password, and tell a grown-up. Report it if you can.

steps.say: A message in Online City: "FREE GOLD! 1000 gold for you! Send your password to get it." What do you press?
steps.done: Closed. Then you tell a grown-up and report it.

safe_mistake.wrong: clicking a free gold offer that wants your password
safe_mistake.why: It's a scam: a trick to take your account and everything in it. Real games never ask for your password.
safe_mistake.right: Close it, never give your password, and tell a grown-up. Report it if you can.

steps.say: Free gold, if you send your password. What do you press?
steps.done: Closed, all by yourself.

steps.say: A message that looks like the game's: "Your account will close today! Log in at this link." You...

choices.text: Don't click: open the game yourself and ask a grown-up

choices.why: Messages that rush you are often tricks. Never log in from a link in a message.

steps.done: No click. Tricks like that are called phishing.

steps.say: Kiki makes a password. This game's rules: at least 6 letters, never your name, nothing easy to guess. Which follows them?

choices.text: Make it two words and a number that only Kiki would think of

choices.why: Never your name, even with numbers.
A row of keys is far too easy to guess.
Too short: at least 6 letters.

steps.done: Long, not her name, hard to guess.

steps.say: Your best friend asks for your password to help you get to the next level. You say...

choices.text: Never tell anyone your password. Not even a friend.
Share it with your best friend
choices.why: A shared password isn't secret any more. Never tell anyone, not even a friend.

steps.done: Your password, your secret.

steps.say: This game protects you too: after 5 wrong tries in 15 minutes it makes a guesser wait, and logging in on a new device logs the old one out at once.
A story: "Ice cream will be banned next week!" Before you share it, check: who made it, when, and does anyone else say so?
steps.done: No maker, no date, nobody else says so: don't share it.

steps.say: A story: "Schools will open at midnight from now on!" Check it before you share it.
steps.done: Checked by yourself: it isn't true.

steps.say: The story's picture shows a cat as big as a bus. Is it real?

choices.text: A picture can be changed: check where it comes from

choices.why: Apps can change a picture in seconds. Check where it comes from.

steps.done: A changed picture. Good thinking.

steps.say: A group chat laughs at Bobo's dance video and asks you to add a joke. You...

choices.text: Don't join in: be kind to Bobo, report it, tell a grown-up

choices.why: Even if everyone is, joining in hurts. Stand by Bobo and tell someone.

steps.done: You stood by Bobo. That takes courage.

steps.say: An hour before bed, you...

choices.text: Put the tablet away and wind down

choices.why: Screens before bed make sleep harder. Charge it outside the bedroom.

steps.done: Better sleep, and the game is there tomorrow.

steps.say: Private things stay private, scams and phishing are spotted, passwords are strong and secret, news is checked, pictures can be changed, and you stand by a friend. Expert online!

check.say: A free gold offer wants your password. It's...

choices.text: A scam: close it and tell

check.say: Before you share a news story, you...

choices.text: Check who, when and if others say so

check.say: A message says: log in at this link, now! You...

choices.text: Don't click: open the game yourself

name_it.title: Private, checked, secret
lines: Your school, your address, photos of you and your password stay private. Think before you post.
Free prizes that want your password are scams; links that rush you are phishing. Close them, tell, report.
News: who made it, when, does anyone else say so? A picture can be changed.
A strong password: long, never your name, never shared, not even with a friend.
name_it.source: the UK Safer Internet Centre, Childnet, the NSPCC, UNICEF and the UK's National Cyber Security Centre

big.try_real: With a grown-up, check the privacy settings of an app you use, and look at one news story together: who made it, when, and does anyone else say so?

sources.fact: Scams and phishing: be wary of messages that offer free things, rush you or ask for passwords; never log in from a link in a message; report it and tell a trusted adult.
sources.source: UK Safer Internet Centre, scams and phishing

sources.fact: Use long passwords (three random words) that you don't use anywhere else, and never share them.
sources.source: the UK's National Cyber Security Centre, Cyber Aware

sources.fact: Your digital footprint: what you post can be copied, shared and found later; keep your school, address and photos private and use privacy settings.
Check information before sharing: who made it, when, and whether trusted sources agree; pictures and videos can be edited.
Stand by someone being bullied online: don't join in, support them, report it and tell a trusted adult.
The game's own brake (owner #105): after 5 wrong password tries in 15 minutes a guesser waits; logging in on another device logs the old one out.
